neighbours.label: the setup right before a statistic is given: an estimate or a superlative/endangered claim about to be quantified ('scientists estimate that', 'the leading cause of X,' 'critically endangered,'), as against the same claims that are not followed by a number
fire: Stroke is the second leading cause of death, accounting for about 11 percent of deaths.
Researchers estimate that roughly 40 percent of the reef has already died.
The vaquita is critically endangered, with only about ten animals remaining.
Economists estimate that the flood cost the region two billion dollars.
Malaria is the deadliest disease in the region, killing 400,000 people a year.
Experts estimate that it takes six months to train a new pilot.
The snow leopard is endangered, with fewer than 7,000 left in the wild.
Lung cancer is the most common cancer worldwide, making up 12 percent of cases.
quiet: Stroke is a medical emergency that needs treatment within hours.
Researchers believe that the reef is home to colourful fish.
The vaquita is a small porpoise that lives in the Gulf of California.
Economists say that the flood damaged roads and bridges in the region.
Malaria is spread by mosquitoes that bite at night.
Experts say that training a new pilot is hard work.
The snow leopard is a large cat that lives in the mountains of Asia.
Lung cancer is often linked to smoking and air pollution.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.5 on ' estimate' or on the comma after a superlative claim; plain descriptive sentences without a statistic below 0.25
short: setup before a statistic (estimate that, leading cause,)
notes: Card: commas after 'most serious', 'verge of collapse', 'most common cause of kidney failure', 'critically endangered', then the statistic; also ' estimated', ' would' in 'predicts that it would take 170 years'. Probe: 'critically endangered,' 0.510, 'leading cause of death,' 0.461, 'Scientists estimate' 0.453, 'close to collapse,' 0.240, 'predicts' 0.221. Leaks: 'a serious illness, and' 0.326, 'a large animal, with' 0.247, so the comma alone carries a lot; near misses here drop the comma. 'Scientists think' 0.023. Low confidence; may fail on leaks.
